summary: Carcassonne Big Box 6 is the classic tile-laying game bundled with its most beloved expansions, so it plays like familiar Carcassonne but with more variety from farmers, traders, rivers, and inns and cathedrals mixed in. It's simple to teach, quick to play, and scales from a light two-player game to a chaotic multiplayer scramble for territory.
praised: great expansion content that adds meaningful variety without complexity spikes
high production value bundling in one box
criticised: base game can feel too simple or repetitive for hobbyists
meeple placement luck of the tile draw can frustrate planners
farmer scoring can be fiddly and swingy

interaction.kind: tile placement and area majority contests
interaction.detail: Players place tiles onto a shared, ever-growing map and place meeples to claim roads, cities, cloisters, and fields, directly contesting the same features for majority control. The map is entirely communal while each player's meeples and score are tracked individually.

subsystems: tile & meeple placement scoring (roads, cities, monasteries, farms — including Inns & Cathedrals' higher-stakes big roads/cities)
trade goods majority scoring (wine/cloth/grain, from Traders & Builders)
gold bar accumulation scoring (from The Gold Mines)
sources: completed roads (1 pt/tile, 2 with an inn)
completed cities (2 pts/tile+shield, 3 with a cathedral)
incomplete features at game end (1 pt/tile)
farms scored at game end (3 pts per adjacent completed city, majority)
trade goods majority bonus (10 pts each for most wine/cloth/grain)
scoring.how_you_win: Players place tiles and meeples to claim roads, cities, monasteries and farms, scoring roads/cities/monasteries as soon as they're completed and farms plus trade-goods and gold-bar bonuses only at the end; when the tile supply runs out the game ends and the highest total wins.
